mainTopic: Work on חול המועד: a layman's work versus a craftsman's work, repairs and preserving food in the משנה, preventing a loss, and the end of the first chapter.
overview: This amud finishes the first chapter of מועד קטן, which is about work on חול המועד. It opens with the end of a ברייתא: buying at a gentile fair counts as rescuing property, so a chance you will lose is treated like a loss. Stories follow. רב allows simple traps, which are a layman's work (מעשה הדיוט), but not nets, which are a craftsman's work (מעשה אומן). רב יהודה allows building ovens, but only in summer, when the oven will be ready for the festival. A new משנה then allows simple repairs: a railing, oven cracks smoothed by hand or foot, broken door parts, and pickling food that can be eaten during the festival. The גמרא explains each line. To settle a clash with the hammering that stopped in ירושלים, it brings several answers and concludes that in practice we follow רבי יוסי, who allows normal work to prevent a loss. A story about רבא letting people salt fish leads to fish-eating tips from רב, and the chapter ends with הדרן.

steps.title: Buying at a gentile fair counts as rescuing property
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: one may buy animals, slaves, land and houses at a gentile fair and register the deeds in their courts, because it is like rescuing from their hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One may go] to a fair of gentiles and buy animals, slaves and maidservants, houses, fields and vineyards. One may write the deeds and confirm them in their courts, because it is like rescuing [property] from their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא about buying things at a gentile fair. It uses this source to show that a chance you will lose counts like a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally going to a gentile fair, or using their courts, could be a problem. The ברייתא allows it because the buyer will not get this chance again, so buying now is like saving his property. That idea supports treating a time-sensitive deal as a case of real loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Confirms or registers a document in court

phrases.english: to a fair of gentiles,
and buy animals, slaves and maidservants,
houses, fields and vineyards,
and he may write [the deeds] and confirm [them] in their courts,
because it is as if he is rescuing [it] from their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that began just before this part of the daf.
steps.raayaObject: A deal that will not come again counts as a financial loss.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about buying at a gentile fair, explained as 'like rescuing from their hands'.

steps.title: רב allows weaving simple traps on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב allowed חייא בר אשי to weave simple traps on חול המועד, because it is a layman's work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב permitted חייא בר אשי to weave traps on חול המועד. What is the reason? It is a layman's work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: רב let someone weave simple traps on חול המועד. It then explains the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is that work any ordinary person can do (מעשה הדיוט) is allowed on חול המועד. Simple traps are easy to make, so they fall into this group.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of the festival
A layman's work, which any ordinary person can do

phrases.english: Rav permitted Ḥiyya bar Ashi
to weave traps on the intermediate days of the festival.
What is the reason? It is a layman's work,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about which kinds of work are allowed on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weaving simple traps is allowed on חול המועד because it is a layman's work.

steps.title: Nets are forbidden because they are a craftsman's work
steps.stepSummary: Nets are not allowed, because making them is a craftsman's work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But nets are forbidden. What is the reason? It is a craftsman's work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a limit on רב's permission. Nets, unlike simple traps, may not be made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nets take skill to make, so they count as מעשה אומן. This contrast shows that the line is drawn by how much skill the work needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Nets, which are complex to make
A craftsman's work, which needs skill

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, a layman's work (מעשה הדיוט) is allowed, but a craftsman's work (מעשה אומן) is forbidden. Simple traps are allowed, nets are not.

phrases.english: But nets are forbidden.
What is the reason? It is a craftsman's work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of the permission given in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making nets is forbidden on חול המועד because it is a craftsman's work.

steps.title: רב יהודה allows making ovens and sieves
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה allowed אמי the oven maker to build ovens, and רבה בר עשבי to make sieves, on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה permitted אמי the oven maker to build ovens, and רבה בר עשבי to make sieves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story of permission on חול המועד, this time for ovens and sieves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This permission is surprising, because building an oven sounds like real construction. That makes it a natural target for the challenge that comes next.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה שְׁרָא לְאַמֵּי תַּנּוּרָאָה לְמִיגְדַּל תַּנּוּרֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda permitted Ami the oven maker to build ovens,
phrases.notes: 'Build' here is literally 'weave'. These clay ovens were built up out of rolled coils.

phrases.english: and Rabba bar Ashabi to make sieves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story of permission, similar to רב's story in steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building ovens and making sieves were permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא that forbids building an oven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this can be, since רבה בר שמואל taught that everyone agrees one may not build a new oven on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? Didn't רבה בר שמואל teach: And they agree that one may not build an oven from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's permission to build ovens. It quotes a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says even the opinions that usually argue all agree that a new oven may not be built. That seems to clash directly with רב יהודה letting אמי build ovens.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] teach in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי? וְהָא תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rabba bar Shmuel teach:
And they agree that one may not build an oven from the start!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the permission to build ovens given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's permission for אמי to build ovens.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says everyone agrees a new oven may not be built on חול המועד, which contradicts the permission.

steps.title: Summer versus the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. רב יהודה's permission was for the summer, and the ברייתא's ban is for the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is in the summer, there it is in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the two sources into two different seasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In hot summer weather a new oven dries quickly and can be used during the festival itself, so building it is allowed. In the rainy season it will not be ready in time, so building it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: A new oven may be built on חול המועד in the summer, when it can be used during the festival, but not in the rainy season.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here, in the summer;
phrases.notes: 'Here' is רב יהודה's permission, when the oven dries fast and is ready for the festival.

phrases.english: there, in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה כָּאן בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into different cases (different seasons)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid building ovens at all times, against רב יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה allowed it in summer, when the oven is usable during the festival. The ברייתא forbids it in the rainy season.

steps.title: משנה: a railing may be built only in a simple way
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that one may build a railing for a roof or balcony on חול המועד as a layman's work, but not as a craftsman's work.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may make a railing for a roof or a balcony as a layman's work, but not as a craftsman's work.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows building a safety railing on חול המועד, but only in a simple, non-professional way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the same line we just saw in רב's ruling: מעשה הדיוט is allowed, מעשה אומן is not. A railing is needed for safety, but it still may not be done in a skilled way.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה; marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may make a railing for a roof or for a balcony

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂה הֶדְיוֹט, אֲבָל לֹא מַעֲשֵׂה אוּמָּן.
phrases.english: as a layman's work, but not as a craftsman's work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It uses the same layman versus craftsman line seen in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A railing may be built on חול המועד only in a simple, layman's way.

steps.title: משנה: smoothing oven cracks by hand or foot, not with a tool
steps.stepSummary: One may plaster cracks in an oven and smooth them with a roller, by hand or foot, but not with a presser.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may plaster the cracks and smooth them with a roller, with a hand or a foot, but not with a presser.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another repair: fixing cracks in an oven. Simple ways are allowed, but a special professional tool is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using your hand or foot is a layman's way of fixing the cracks. The מחלצים is a tool made for this job, so using it is a professional way of working and is forbidden. The mention of a roller seems odd here, and the גמרא takes this up in steps 14–15.

keyTerms.meaning: A presser, a special tool made for this work

phrases.english: One may plaster the cracks
and smooth them over with a roller,
with a hand or a foot, but not with a presser.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁפִין אֶת הַסְּדָקִין וּמַעֲגִילִין אוֹתָן בַּמַּעֲגִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second case of the same layman versus craftsman idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oven cracks may be fixed in a simple way by hand or foot, but not with a professional presser.

steps.title: Fixing broken door parts on the holiday
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows fixing a broken hinge, beam, lock or key on חול המועד, as long as the person did not put off the repair on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hinge, its socket, the door beam, a lock or a key that broke may be fixed on חול המועד, as long as he did not plan to do this work during the מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of jobs allowed on חול המועד. It permits repairing broken parts of a door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken door or lock is a real need during the holiday, so the repair is allowed. The condition blocks a trick: a person may not purposely save a job for חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: provided that he does not intend (to push off the work)

phrases.english: The hinge, the hinge-socket, and the beam
and the lock and the key that broke
one may fix them on the Festival
provided that he does not intend
to do his work on the Festival

steps.triggerLanguage: הַצִּיר וְהַצִּינּוֹר וְהַקּוֹרָה וְהַמַּנְעוּל וְהַמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the מתניתין's list of permitted repairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broken door parts may be fixed on חול המועד, unless the work was deliberately delayed until then.

steps.title: Pickling food that will be ready during the holiday
steps.stepSummary: Any pickled food that will be ready to eat during the מועד may be pickled on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any pickled foods that he will be able to eat during the מועד, he may pickle.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with one more permission: preparing pickled foods on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the food will be ready to eat during the holiday itself. If it will, the work counts as a holiday need and is permitted.

phrases.english: And all pickled foods
that he can eat from on the Festival
he may pickle them

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל כְּבָשִׁין שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לֶאֱכוֹל מֵהֶן בַּמּוֹעֵד כּוֹבְשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last ruling of the מתניתין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pickling is allowed on חול המועד if the food will be edible during the holiday.

steps.title: What counts as a layman's railing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking what exactly 'layman's work' means for the roof railing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is considered layman's work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion. It asks for a definition of the 'layman's work' that the משנה allowed for a railing (step 7). This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה drew a line between layman's work, which is allowed, and craftsman's work, which is forbidden, but it never said where that line falls. The גמרא wants a practical picture.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? / how do we picture it?

phrases.english: Gemara
What are the circumstances of layman's work?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the railing for a roof or balcony from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the railing rule of step 7 to define its terms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of a layman-style railing.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a railing of branches
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says a layman's railing is one made of palm and bay branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: with palm branches and bay branches.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by describing a railing made of branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches make a simple, makeshift barrier, not a permanent built wall, so building one does not count as professional construction.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said
with palm branches and bay branches

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A layman's railing is made of palm and bay branches.

steps.title: A ברייתא: stones without plaster
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one may fill in the railing with stones but may not plaster them with clay.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: he fills in with stones, but does not plaster with clay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another picture of a layman's railing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stacking loose stones is simple work. Plastering them with clay turns the railing into a real, solid wall, and that is craftsman's work.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita
he fills in with stones
but he does not plaster with clay

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא צָר בִּצְרוֹר וְאֵינוֹ טָח בְּטִיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, ברייתא-based description alongside רב יוסף's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Loose stones are allowed; plastering them with clay is not.
steps.whatToRemember: Layman's work means a simple, makeshift railing: branches, or stones without plaster.

steps.title: Why mention hand and foot after a roller?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the oven rule and asks: if a roller is allowed, why say hand and foot are allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may plaster the cracks and smooth them with a roller.' Now, if you say a roller is permitted, is it even necessary to say a hand or foot is?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the oven-plastering line of the משנה (step 8) and points out that its wording seems strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A roller is a tool, so using it seems like more of a 'craftsman's' act than using a hand or foot. If the tool is allowed, the hand and foot are obviously allowed, so it looks pointless for the משנה to list them.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule. The גמרא is re-quoting the משנה from step 8 only to question its wording.

phrases.english: One may plaster the cracks
and smooth them with a roller
Now, with a roller you say it is permitted
with a hand or foot, is it necessary to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בְּמַעֲגִילָה אָמְרַתְּ שְׁרֵי בַּיָּד וּבָרֶגֶל מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and questions its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה's oven rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the more tool-like roller is permitted, listing hand and foot adds nothing.

steps.title: Like a roller, using hand or foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה means smoothing the cracks the way a roller would, using a hand or a foot, but not with a presser.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: one may plaster the cracks and smooth them like a roller, with the hand or foot, but not with a presser.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the משנה. 'Roller' describes the kind of motion, not an actual tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No real roller is allowed at all. One may only make a rolling motion with a hand or foot. The professional tool, the presser, stays forbidden because using it is craftsman's work.

keyTerms.meaning: a presser, a craftsman's smoothing tool

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, oven cracks may be smoothed only by hand or foot in a rolling motion, never with a professional tool.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying
one may plaster the cracks
and smooth them as if with a roller
with the hand or the foot
but not with a presser

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow an actual roller tool.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Roller' describes a rolling motion done by hand or foot; real tools are not allowed.

steps.title: Our משנה: broken door parts may be fixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from our משנה that allows fixing broken door parts on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a hinge, its cylinder, a crossbeam, a lock or a key broke, you may fix them on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. It is setting up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repairing these items is real work, yet the משנה allows it on חול המועד. Keep this permission in mind, because the next source seems to say the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: Beam (here, the crossbeam that holds the door)
חול המועד, the intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: The hinge, and the cylinder, and the crossbeam
phrases.notes: The צִינּוֹר is the round piece that the hinge turns in.

phrases.english: and the lock and the key that broke
one may fix them on the intermediate days of the Festival

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה after finishing the discussion of the railing and the oven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broken door parts, locks and keys may be repaired on חול המועד.

steps.title: Contradiction from the hammering in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that hammers were heard in ירושלים only until the days of יוחנן כהן גדול, which implies that such work was later banned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a different משנה says: until his days, hammers would bang in ירושלים. So until then yes, but from then on no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה that seems to forbid repair work on חול המועד, which clashes with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'until his days' imply that after יוחנן כהן גדול, hammering on חול המועד was stopped. If repair work is banned, how can our משנה allow fixing broken door parts?

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: introduces a source that clashes with ours

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction
Until his days a hammer would
phrases.notes: 'His days' means the days of יוחנן כהן גדול, from a משנה in מעשר שני.

phrases.english: beat in Jerusalem, etc.
Until his days, yes
from then on, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the permission in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's permission to repair broken door parts on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From 'until his days' we learn that hammering work was later forbidden on חול המועד, so repair work should be forbidden.

steps.title: Smiths versus carpenters
steps.stepSummary: The ban is on noisy smiths' work. The permission is for quieter carpenters' work.
steps.simpleTranslation: No problem: one source speaks about smiths and the other about carpenters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources speak about different kinds of workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smiths bang loudly, so their work was stopped. Carpenters make less noise, so fixing a door with carpentry is allowed.

phrases.english: This is not difficult
In one case it is about smiths
in the other case it is about carpenters

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּדְנַפָּחֵי, כָּאן בִּדְנַגָּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of worker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to speak about the same kind of repair work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Loud smith work is banned, and quieter carpentry is allowed.

steps.title: רב חסדא: people will think only noise matters
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the smith/carpenter answer, because people would conclude that only loud work is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objects: people will say a loud noise is forbidden but a soft noise is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the answer from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule depended on how loud the work is, people would think the issue is only noise and not the work itself. That would be a misleading message, so the answer cannot stand.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda strongly objects to this
People will say
a loud noise is forbidden
a soft noise is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 18.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Making the rule depend on volume would send the wrong message about what is forbidden.

steps.title: רב חסדא: sickles versus chisels
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא offers his own answer: one source speaks about sickles and the other about chisels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא says: no problem. This one is about sickles, that one is about chisels.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the earlier answer, רב חסדא gives a different split between the two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permitted case involves sickles, which make no noise at all. The forbidden case involves chisels. So the line is not about 'loud versus soft'.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said
It is not difficult
This one is about sickles
that one is about chisels

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 18 with a new answer to step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of tool
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split was between loud and quiet workers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Work with sickles is permitted, and work with chisels is forbidden.

steps.title: רב פפא: before and after the decree
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the two sources reflect two time periods, before and after the decree of יוחנן כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: one source is from before the decree, the other is from after the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another way to settle the contradiction, based on time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה's permission reflects the law before יוחנן כהן גדול's decree. The other משנה reflects the law after the decree, when hammering stopped.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said
Here, it is before the decree
there, it is after the decree
phrases.notes: The decree is the one of יוחנן כהן גדול that stopped the hammering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כָּאן — קוֹדֶם גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the contradiction in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to describe the same time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission is from before the decree and the ban is from after it.

steps.title: רב אשי: a debate between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the two sources follow different תנאים: the ban follows רבי יהודה and the permission follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: that one follows רבי יהודה, and this one follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי settles the contradiction by saying the two משניות follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No need to find different cases. The two sources simply follow a real disagreement: רבי יהודה is stricter, and רבי יוסי is more lenient.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said
That one follows Rabbi Yehuda
this one follows Rabbi Yosei

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָא — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא — רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the contradiction in step 17, alongside those of רב חסדא and רב פפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to reflect one shared opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban follows רבי יהודה and our משנה's permission follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Support: רבי יוסי is lenient about a loss
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי shows that requiring a change in how work is done, even to prevent a loss, is not רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: who taught that work on חול המועד needs a change even to prevent a loss? Not רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אשי by showing that רבי יוסי is lenient about work done to prevent a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some taught that even to prevent a loss, one must work in an unusual way on חול המועד. רבי יצחק בר אבדימי says this is not רבי יוסי. So רבי יוסי allows normal work to prevent a loss, which fits our משנה's permission to fix broken door parts.

keyTerms.meaning: A change: doing work in an unusual way
Something that will be lost if not dealt with now
A sage of the משנה period

steps.whatToRemember: The first answer, smiths versus carpenters, was rejected by רב חסדא. Three answers remain that settle the contradiction: sickles versus chisels (רב חסדא), before versus after the decree (רב פפא), and רבי יהודה versus רבי יוסי (רב אשי). רבי יוסי allows normal work to prevent a loss.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi said
Who is the tanna who taught that work on the Festival needs a change
even for something that will be lost
It is not like Rabbi Yosei

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's claim that רבי יוסי is the lenient view.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the permitting משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's statement that requiring a change even for a loss is not רבי יוסי's view

steps.title: Our practice of lifting the door lintel follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that people's current practice of lifting a door lintel on חול המועד in the normal way follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Whose opinion are we following today when we lift up the beam over a door on חול המועד? We are following רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא connects a real-life practice to the מחלוקת just discussed. He says the common habit follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step we saw that רבי יוסי does not require changing how you do work when it prevents a loss. Lifting the lintel the normal way on חול המועד only makes sense under his view. So רבינא shows that our practice follows רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the in-between days of the festival

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, we follow רבי יוסי: work that prevents a loss may be done in the normal way on חול המועד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב אשי's answer (two תנאים) has real practical weight. The accepted practice follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
In accordance with whom do we nowadays lift up
the lintels of the door
on the intermediate days of the Festival?
In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion that רבי יוסי allows normal-way work to prevent a loss to a real practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lifting a door lintel on חול המועד in the normal way follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The משנה's rule about pickling on the מועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: you may pickle foods on the מועד if you can eat from them during the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: pickled foods that a person can eat during the festival may be pickled on the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has a built-in limit: you may pickle only what you can use during the מועד itself. Pickling for after the festival is not allowed. Keep this limit in mind, because the next story tests it.

phrases.english: Preserved foods that he is able
to eat on the Festival, he may preserve them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָשִׁין שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לֶאֱכוֹל בַּמּוֹעֵד כּוֹבְשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pickling on the מועד is allowed only for food that can be eaten during the מועד.

steps.title: רבא allows salting the fish from the river
steps.stepSummary: The בדיתא river washed up many fish, everyone caught them, and רבא allowed them to salt some of the fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בדיתא river overflowed and left fish behind. Everyone went, caught fish, and brought them home. רבא allowed them to salt some of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story with a ruling from רבא. He let people salt fish on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salting fish is a kind of preserving. People had far more fish than they could eat during the festival. So רבא's ruling seems to go beyond the משנה's limit, and that sets up אביי's challenge.

phrases.english: The Bedita river cast up fish;
phrases.notes: Literally, the river 'spat out' fish. It overflowed and left fish on the banks.

phrases.english: everyone went,
trapped and brought fish,
and Rava permitted them
to salt some of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that tests the משנה's pickling rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא permitted salting the fish that were caught on חול המועד.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the משנה only allows preserving food you can eat during the מועד, and these fish were too many to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: But we learned in the משנה that you may pickle only foods you can eat from during the festival!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's ruling by quoting the משנה back to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows preserving only for festival use. These fish were far more than anyone could eat during the festival. So salting them seems to be preserving for after the festival, which the משנה forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (introduces a challenge from a משנה)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But didn't we learn:
Preserved foods that he is able
to eat from on the Festival, he may preserve them!
phrases.notes: The hidden point: these fish were too many to eat during the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling from step 26 using the משנה from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission to salt the fish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה limits preserving to food that will be eaten during the מועד. These fish were more than that, so salting them should be forbidden.

steps.title: The fish count as merchandise about to be lost
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the fish were brought to be eaten, and without salting they would spoil, so this counts as preventing a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since they first brought the fish meaning to eat them, and if they leave them the fish will spoil, it is like merchandise that is about to be lost, so it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling. He moves the case into a different category: preventing a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees with the משנה's rule. He says it does not apply here. The fish were caught in a permitted way, for eating. If they are left alone they will rot, so salting them is like saving goods from being lost, which is allowed on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Merchandise that is about to be lost

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the משנה's limit is wrong. He is saying this case belongs to a different rule, the rule of preventing a loss.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since from the start
they brought them with the intention of eating,
and if one leaves them, they will spoil,
it is like merchandise that is being lost,
and it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כֵּיוָן דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא אַדַּעְתָּא דַאֲכִילָה אַיְיתִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the case into a different legal category (preventing a loss)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Salting extra fish is forbidden preserving for after the festival.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the fish were brought to be eaten and would spoil, salting them counts as preventing a loss, so it is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Food that was caught for the festival and would otherwise spoil can be saved like merchandise about to be lost.

steps.title: A second version: רבא allowed catching and salting
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבא went further. He allowed people to go catch the fish, bring them, and salt them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the story went differently: רבא allowed them to catch the fish, go bring them, and salt them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story. Here רבא's permission covers the whole process from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the fish were not first brought for eating. So רבא's answer from step 28 cannot be used here. The question is whether such a broad permission fits the משנה.

phrases.english: And some say:
Rava permitted them
to trap, to go bring, and to salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the story from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא permitted catching, bringing and salting the fish.

steps.title: אביי challenges the second version too
steps.stepSummary: אביי again quotes the משנה. You may preserve only what can be eaten during the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But we learned that you may pickle only foods you can eat from during the festival!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי raises the same challenge against this second version. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the fish were caught with the plan of salting them. Heavily salted fish seem unfit to eat until they have fully cured, so they would not be food for the festival. That clashes directly with the משנה's limit, and the earlier answer about fish first brought for eating does not apply.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But we,
'preserved foods that he is able to eat from,
he may preserve them,' we learned!
phrases.notes: In this version the fish were salted heavily, so they could not be eaten during the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second version of רבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission to catch and salt the fish in the second version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These fish were salted for after the festival and could not be eaten during it, so the משנה should forbid preserving them.

steps.title: Salted fish can be eaten right away by pressing
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that freshly salted fish can be eaten right away once the salt is pressed out, so they count as food for the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: These fish can also be eaten, by pressing them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge from Step 30. He says the salted fish can also be eaten during the מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the משנה only allows preserving food that can be eaten during the מועד. רבא says freshly salted fish meet that rule, because pressing out the salt and brine makes them ready to eat now. So he did not go beyond what the משנה allows.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressing (squeezing out the salt and brine)

phrases.english: He said to him: These too can be eaten
phrases.notes: רבא is answering אביי. "These" means the fish that were just salted.

phrases.english: by means of pressing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי נָמֵי מִיתְאַכְלִי אַגַּב אִיצָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the salted fish really do count as food eaten during the מועד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Freshly salted fish cannot be eaten until they cure, so salting them is only for after the מועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pressing makes them ready to eat at once, so they fit the משנה's rule.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל, who ate pressed fish
steps.stepSummary: Fish was pressed sixty times for שמואל, and then he ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of שמואל, for whom they pressed fish sixty times and he ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his answer with a story about שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might doubt that freshly salted fish can really be eaten. The story shows a real case: after the fish was pressed many times, שמואל ate it. So pressing really does make salted fish ready to eat.

phrases.english: As in that case of שמואל:
they pressed it for him sixty times and he ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer in Step 31 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that freshly salted fish can be eaten after pressing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ate fish that had been pressed sixty times.

steps.title: רבא ate pressed fish at the ריש גלותא's house
steps.stepSummary: At the house of the ריש גלותא, fish was pressed sixty times for רבא, and he ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא came to the house of the ריש גלותא. They pressed fish for him sixty times and he ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story, this time about רבא himself eating pressed salted fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the שמואל story. It shows that רבא himself had seen and eaten salted fish made ready this way, so his answer comes from real experience.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in בבל

phrases.english: Rava happened to come to the house of the Exilarch,
they pressed it for him sixty times, and he ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story like the שמואל story, about רבא himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freshly salted fish, pressed many times, was eaten by רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: In the second version (איכא דאמרי), רבא's answer is that salting the fish was allowed because pressing makes freshly salted fish ready to eat right away, so it counts as food for the מועד.

steps.title: רב is served a fish made three ways
steps.stepSummary: At רב שפיר's house, רב was served one fish: a third cooked, a third salted, and a third broiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב came to the house of רב שפיר. They brought him a fish that was one-third cooked, one-third salted, and one-third broiled.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is now eating fish, the גמרא moves to a related story. It also sets up the next steps, which are fish tips from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer about the laws of the מועד. It is a side story that follows from the topic of fish. One part was salted, much like the pressed fish just mentioned.

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to the house of Rav Shapir,
they brought before them a certain fish,
one-third cooked, one-third salted,
and one-third broiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side story connected only by the topic of eating fish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single fish was served prepared three different ways.

steps.title: Fish is best just before it spoils
steps.stepSummary: רב quotes אדא ציידא: a fish that is close to spoiling is at its best.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: אדא the fisherman told me that a fish close to spoiling is best.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a list of fish tips that רב learned from a fisherman named אדא. This is the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is practical food advice, not a הלכה. A fish that has sat for a while, right before it goes bad, tastes best.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא,
phrases.english: Rav said: Adda the fisherman told me:
A fish close to its spoiling is best.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of fish with advice from רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish tastes best when it is close to spoiling.

steps.title: Brother, father, and son: how to prepare fish
steps.stepSummary: Broil fish with salt (its brother), put it in water (its father), eat it with brine (its son), and drink water (its father) after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: אדא the fisherman told me: Broil a fish with its brother, place it in its father, eat it with its son, and drink its father after it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a second tip from אדא, written as a riddle using family words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each family word stands for something connected to the fish. Salt is its "brother" because both come from the sea. Water is its "father" because fish come from water, and brine is its "son" because brine comes out of the fish.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this literally. "Brother," "father," and "son" are a riddle for salt, water, and brine.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב, אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא:
phrases.english: And Rav said: Adda the fisherman told me:
A fish: broil it with its brother,
place it in its father,
eat it with its son,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording; it just makes it read "eat it."

phrases.english: drink after it its father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב, אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second fish tip from the same source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broil fish with salt, put it in water, eat it with brine, and drink water after it.

steps.title: Walk, don't sleep, after fish, cress, and milk
steps.stepSummary: After eating fish, cress, and milk, one should walk around rather than go straight to bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: אדא the fisherman told me: After fish, cress, and milk, let the body carry them and not the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a third health tip from אדא, this time about what to do after eating certain foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Let the body carry them" means stay up and walk around. "Not the bed" means don't lie down to sleep right after eating these foods.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב, אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא:
phrases.english: And Rav said: Adda the fisherman told me:
Fish, cress, and milk:
let the body carry them and let not the bed carry them.
phrases.notes: He means: go walk around after eating them, rather than going right to sleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב, אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third tip from the same source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After fish, cress, and milk, walk around instead of lying down.

steps.title: What to drink after fish, cress, and milk
steps.stepSummary: After fish, cress, and milk, drink water rather than beer, and beer rather than wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: אדא the fisherman told me: After fish, cress, and milk, drink water and not beer, beer and not wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a final tip from אדא about the best drink after these foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water is the best choice. If there is no water, beer is better than wine.
steps.whatToRemember: The side topic ends with four fish tips that רב learned from אדא ציידא: fish is best near spoiling; eat it with salt, water, and brine; walk around afterward; and drink water rather than beer, and beer rather than wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב, אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא:
phrases.english: And Rav said: Adda the fisherman told me:
Fish, cress, and milk:
water and not beer,
beer and not wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב, אֲמַר לִי אַדָּא צַיָּידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last tip in the list, about the same three foods as Step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After fish, cress, and milk, drink water before beer, and beer before wine.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing משקין בית השלחין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the first chapter of מועד קטן with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'משקין בית השלחין.'
steps.whatsHappening: Nothing new is being argued here. The גמרא is marking the end of the first chapter of מועד קטן with the traditional farewell line, הדרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chapter in the גמרא is named by its first words, so this one is called 'משקין בית השלחין', the opening words of the first משנה about watering a field that needs irrigation. The הדרן line is a promise and a prayer that we will come back and learn this chapter again. It ends the chapter, so no הלכה or question carries over into the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The traditional words said when finishing a chapter or a מסכת.
We may water (irrigate). The first word of the chapter.
A thirsty field that depends on irrigation, unlike a field that gets enough rain.
A chapter of the משנה or גמרא, usually named by its opening words.

steps.whatToRemember: The first chapter of מועד קטן, משקין בית השלחין, is now finished. A new chapter starts right after this line.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'משקין בית השלחין' are not a new law here. They are just the name of the chapter being closed, taken from its first line.

phrases.english: We will return to you
"We may water an irrigated field" (the chapter's name)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole chapter after the last statements of practical advice about eating fish (steps 34–38).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first chapter of מועד קטן, משקין בית השלחין, is complete.
